newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian minister bullish on June CPI figures.
newsitem.headline: Australian minister bullish on June CPI figures.

text.p: Australian industrial relations and small business minister Peter Reith said on Sunday he would not be surprised if the June quarter inflation rate would show a negative figure when it is released on Wednesday.

"Intuitively some of the numbers have been moving that way as I understand them. I don't focus on them perhaps as closely as I should, but that wouldn't surprise me," Reith told the Face to Face television programme on Seven Network.
The June quarter consumer price index is forecast to fall 0.1 percent in the quarter, and rise 0.5 percent over the year.

If the CPI is negative, it will be the first quarter of deflation since June 1992, and the lowest annual rate since the year to December quarter 1992. If forecasts are met, financial markets expect a further interest rate cut.

Asked if lower inflation figures would point towards another cut in official rates, Reith said: "We as a government are keen to do all that we can to encourage downward pressure on interest rates, I think we've had a fair bit of success there."
"But, I'm not making any comments on monetary policy," Reith said. The official cash rate is 5.50 percent, having been reduced on four occasions over the past year from a level of 7.50 percent.
"We've seen a two percent drop in interest rates since this government's been in, that's a result of us basically moving to balance the books as we've done," said Reith, a senior government minister.

The Liberal-National coalition government have been in power since March 1996 after defeating a 13-year Labor party administration. "So that's a positive, we'd obviously always like to go further," Reith said.
